title: Warboard Communication Kit — templates & checklist (draft)
document_text:
PURPOSE:
This is a working draft of a compact warboard communication kit for on-call SREs and incident commanders. Contains short, copy-paste-ready templates for: status page entries, customer-facing emails, internal Slack war-room notices, and an internal war-room checklist. Save time during paging and reduce inconsistent messaging.

USAGE NOTES (quick):
- Pick the closest template, fill brackets [] and replace with facts only.
- Do not speculate. If unknown, use 'Investigating' or 'Under investigation'.
- Use short subject lines for customer emails and status page titles.
- Post an initial public status update within 30 minutes for severity >= Sev2.
- Internal updates every 15-30m depending on incident cadence.

ROLES & CONTACTS (defaults):
- Incident Commander (IC): whoever acked page, primary decision maker for comm cadence.
- Communications lead: if available, help craft customer messages and approvals.
- Engineering lead: owns mitigation work and technical summary.
- Support liaison: posts to customer channels and collects impacted customer list.
- Pager duty shortcuts: @oncall-sre, @oncall-platform, #warboard-channel.

INTERNAL WAR-ROOM CHECKLIST (minimal actionable items):
- [ ] Create incident artifact: JIRA ticket / Incident doc (JIRA-SRE-XXXX).
- [ ] Open dedicated war-room Slack channel and invite IC, eng lead, support lead, comms lead.
- [ ] Set initial severity (Sev1/Sev2/Sev3) and state in ticket. Note criteria used.
- [ ] Post initial internal brief (use "Internal template: initial" below).
- [ ] Snapshot: collect metrics, logs, recent deploys, configuration changes, infra events.
- [ ] Identify blast radius and affected product surface (API endpoints, regions, customers).
- [ ] Apply immediate mitigations (roll back, scale, route, disable feature) — log actions.
- [ ] Coordinate customer comms cadence and draft public messages (see templates).
- [ ] Decide on status page visibility and link it in customer messages.
- [ ] Track timeline of actions in incident doc (timestamps, actor, outcome).
- [ ] When stable, prepare resolution message with RCA high-level placeholders.

INTERNAL TEMPLATE: INITIAL (copy-paste friendly)
Subject: [INCIDENT STARTED] <short summary> — IC: @<name>
Message body (Slack):
IC: @<name>
Severity: Sev<1|2|3>
What's happening: Brief 1-2 lines (what service, what user impact)
When it started: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
Current status: Investigating / Mitigating / Identified / Partial Restore
Point people: eng: @<name>, support: @<name>, comms: @<name>
Immediate actions: 1) <action> 2) <action>
Next update: in 15m or asap
Link to incident doc: <link>

INTERNAL TEMPLATE: UPDATE (copy-paste)
IC: @<name> — Update: HH:MM UTC
Summary: one sentence on change since last update
Technical status: short bullet(s)
Customer impact: estimated affected endpoints/customers/regions
Actions taken: bullets with timestamps and actor
Next steps: clear, assign owner and ETA

INTERNAL TEMPLATE: RESOLUTION
IC: @<name> — RESOLVED HH:MM UTC
What changed: short description of fix/mitigation
Impact: current user-facing state (fully restored / partial / degraded)
Root cause (tentative): short phrase (full RCA in postmortem)
Open follow-ups: list (owners and due dates)
Postmortem owner: @<name> — target: <date>

STATUS PAGE TEMPLATE (public)
Title: [Investigating / Partial Outage / Service Disruption] — <service name>
Body (short):
We are aware of an issue affecting <service name> that started at <time UTC>. Customers may experience <symptoms, e.g., increased latencies, 5xx errors, failed embeddings>. Our engineering team is investigating and working on a fix.

What we're doing:
- Brief bullet of mitigation efforts (restarts, scaling, rollback, failover)
- If applicable, temporary workarounds for customers

Affected regions/customers: <list or "All users" / "Specific customers: ...">
Next update: planned in ~30 minutes or sooner
Link to internal incident doc: <optional, redacted link if internal-only>

STATUS PAGE UPDATE (public)
Title: Update — <service name> — <progress: Mitigating / Partial Restore / Investigating>
Body: short summary of new facts and ETA if known. Avoid internal-only details.

CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE: INITIAL (for impacted customers)
Subject: Service disruption impacting <product/endpoint> — <short impacted scope>
Hi <Customer Name>,
We’re currently investigating an issue affecting <product/endpoint> that may cause <impact>. Our engineering team is working to restore full service. We’ll send updates by <time/interval> or as significant changes occur.
If you are experiencing critical business impact and need prioritized assistance, reply to this email and include your account ID.
Thanks for your patience,
The Redwood Inference Team

CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE: UPDATE
Subject: Update — <service name> — <short summary>
Hi <Customer Name>,
Update as of <time>: <one-sentence progress>. Impact: <same/less/worsening> Customers affected: <estimation> Workaround: <if any> ETA: <if known>
We’ll follow up again by <time>.

CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE: RESOLUTION
Subject: Resolved — <service name> — incident started <start time>
Hi <Customer Name>,
The issue affecting <service name> has been resolved as of <time UTC>. Summary: <short explanation of fix>. If you continue to see problems, please contact support or reply to this message. We will publish a full postmortem within <timeframe>.
Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support

SLACK PHRASING / QUICK SNIPPETS (copy):
- "IC: @Aisha — Investigating user-facing 5xxs on /v1/generate. Assessing blast radius."
- "Update HH:MM UTC — Identified root cause candidate: config push to autoscaler. Rolling back."
- "Resolved HH:MM UTC — Service restored. Monitoring for regressions. Postmortem assigned to @Marcus."

DOCUMENTATION & CHECKS BEFORE SENDING CUSTOMER EMAILS
- Verify scope: which customers in which plans are impacted? (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Sanitize logs: do not include PII or internal API keys in messages.
- Consult security/compliance for incidents involving data exposure before sending a public message.

ESCALATION & TIMING RULES (suggested):
- Sev1: post public status within 15-30m; internal updates 10-15m; customer emails if impacted payers.
- Sev2: post public status within 30-60m; internal updates 15-30m.
- Sev3: internal only unless customers affected; manual judgment call.

COMMON PITFALLS (notes to self):
- Avoid promising ETA unless reliable (use ranges).
- Avoid technical jargon in customer messages. Keep to impact + next steps.
- Don't mix speculative root cause in public messages. Use "under investigation" or "likely" qualifiers.

POST-INCIDENT HANDOFF (short):
- IC writes final timeline and tags postmortem owner.
- Postmortem should include: chronology, root cause analysis, mitigations, follow-ups, detection and alerting gaps, and cost impact estimate.
- Communicate postmortem summary to customers if they were impacted.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (working):
- Should we standardize a 30-minute public status SLA for Sev2? pros/cons noted below.
- Need a permissioned status page flow for Dedicated customers with private notices.
- Draft a short one-pager for sales/CS on when to proactively reach out to top accounts.

QUICK LINKS (for war-room):
- Incident runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Incident+Response+Runbook
- Incident template (jira): JIRA-SRE-4321
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.com/dashboard

NOTES (choppy, quick):
- keep templates terse. copy/paste win.
- want 'customer severity' field in incident doc: business-critical / no-impact / partial.
- consider adding a small template for customers on Dedicated with contact engineering CSM/AE in CC.

END OF DRAFT — feedback wanted: @eng-sre channel
